title: Check cited results against their sources
statement: Before acting on a cited result, requirement or analysis of what a test measures, check it against its original source, because summaries merge, move and relabel what they cite.
example: A 13.83% gain in citation grounding was later cited as a "13-50% grounding improvement".
detail: Comparing the AP question work's summaries with the sections they summarise turned up several drifts. A 13.83% gain in citation grounding, with only about half the sentences fully covered (`icloud-work/ML learnings/research_rag_factual_grounding.md`), became an expected "13-50% grounding improvement" in the same summary and "Published results" in the strategy note (`icloud-work/ML learnings/master_strategy_apr24.md`). A 96% validity result belongs to custom-chunked retrieval in one study, but the index credits it to graph retrieval (`icloud-work/ML learnings/research_educational_content_generation.md`, `icloud-work/ML learnings/INDEX.md`). An internal team result was called published, and a verification method's result was cited for a pre-writing step it never tested (`icloud-work/ML learnings/research_qwen3_structured_multistage.md`). For a requirement, the source to check against is the official one.

evidence.quote: Results: Citation grounding improved by **13.83%** on production benchmarks versus standard RAG prompting. However, only ~50% of sentences achieved perfect citation coverage without fine-tuning, suggesting a ceiling that requires SFT to overcome fully.
Expected result: 13-50% grounding improvement based on the SIGIR 2025 paper.

Force the model to emit `[FACT: <exact quote from curriculum_facts>]` before each specific historical claim in scoring notes. Zero cost to try. Published results: 13-50% grounding improvement. Ceiling ~50% without training, but combined with the existing anchor-fact constraint this should push SAQ above 0%.
